name: PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: CPIN — the margin was right, the depreciation was not
frontmatter.summary: The chick-price circular changes no modelled line, but the model behind the call did: the unsourced margin give-back is gone, depreciation is reconciled to its derivation and tax is set to the witnessed rate. The target is Rp5,240 on a total return of 130.9%, and the DCF sits above the price.
thesis: The nine-month result remains an actual, not a forecast — sales of IDR60,200bn against IDR50,600bn and attributable profit of IDR5,180bn — and the chick-price circular changes no modelled line [S2, S11].

The circular keeps the chick ceiling at the farm gate, adds a floor below it and drops the higher ex-factory reference, which is CPIN's own producer-side price; the direction is ambiguous rather than negative [S11, S2].

The margin widened on sourceable arithmetic: cost of goods sold of IDR49,600bn grew by about a sixth against sales growth of nearly a fifth, and we attribute nothing to a corn price the company does not disclose [S2, F1, F2].
Depreciation is 1.5% of sales, the rate its own derivation implies, against the pack's IDR310bn on IDR70,700bn of revenue, and tax is the witnessed rate; both lift the cash-flow value [S0, S2].
The shares trade at 6.9x trailing earnings against a year-high of Rp4,810 and pay Rp233 over the next twelve months, so the de-rating, not the earnings, is the opportunity [S0].

catalysts.event: First full quarter under the DOC final-stock guidance and the new price references
FY2026 audited statements — the first full year to carry the recovered margin and a depreciation note this report can only estimate
Annual general meeting and the FY2026 dividend declaration

blocks.text: Rating BUY, target Rp5,240, a total return of 130.9% from Rp2,370 [S0]. Three things changed in this note and none is the news flow. First, the base case no longer carries a margin give-back: the FY2027E gross-margin input sat far below the FY2026E input while the two years charged identical corn and soymeal values, so the fall was the calibration unwinding, and one convention now runs through every forecast year [S0, S2]. Second, depreciation is reconciled to its own derivation at 1.5% of sales instead of running about a sixth above it, which lowers EBITDA slightly; the restatement alone costs about one hundred and seventy rupiah a share against the margin and tax fixes [S0]. Third, tax is the witnessed rate [S2]. The DCF at Rp4,382 sits above the price [S0].

On 10 November 2026 Bapanas circular No. 456/2026 reset the price references it monitors. For broiler chicks it sets a farm-gate band from Rp6,500 to Rp7,000 per chick, where the previous decision had the same Rp7,000 farm-gate figure plus an ex-factory reference of Rp11,000 [S11]. The ceiling that binds a farmer is unchanged; the floor and the loss of the factory reference are new. The segment reports IDR3,440bn of nine-month revenue and no price per chick, so nothing in the forecast moves [S2, S11].

The same document carries references further up the chain and a ministry request to cut chick final stock by up to 17.0% from 19 October [S11, S13]. We do not convert live weight into carcass weight to manufacture a spread and the pass-through has no published elasticity, so both are directional: we state the direction, leave the possibility in the bull narrative and out of the numbers [S11, S12, S13].

The case rests on reported actuals — sales of IDR60,200bn against IDR50,600bn, profit of IDR5,180bn and earnings per share of Rp316 [S2] — and a 6.9x trailing multiple against a year-high of Rp4,810 [S0]. The discounted cash flow now says Rp4,382, above the Rp2,370 price; the P/E and EV/EBITDA checks say Rp5,035 and Rp5,058; the Rp4,713 base rolled at the cost of equity net of the Rp233 dividend gives Rp5,095, and the 50.0%/25.0%/25.0% base/bear/bull weighting gives the Rp5,240 target [S0]. What moves value: the gross margin, the working-capital intensity, and the multiple the market is willing to pay for earnings that have just grown by half.

CPIN is Indonesia's largest poultry and animal-feed group, integrated from feed mill to plate. Nine-month segment sales were IDR26,980bn from broiler growing, IDR20,740bn from feed, IDR8,150bn from processed chicken, IDR3,440bn from day-old chicks and IDR892bn from other activities, with chicks at IDR3,500bn of a IDR70,700bn top line last year [S2, S5]. Because it sells the feed, the chick and the bird, a lower feed cost reaches it twice [S2].

Sales are domestic: IDR59,940bn inside Indonesia against IDR256bn of exports [S2], so the currency and the global feed complex arrive through costs, not demand [S2, S0]. Control sits in Thailand: the Jiaravanon family holds 55.5% through Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Group, public investors 38.5% and UBS AG Singapore 6.0% [S5].

The chick business is the smallest named segment at IDR3,440bn of nine-month sales [S2]. The statements do not split its sales between third-party farmers and the group's own houses, so we assert no split we cannot source [S2]. Strategy is capacity and integration: in August 2025 it bought breeding facilities from PT Satwa Utama Raya for IDR431bn, a ninety-nine per cent-controlled affiliate, so the deal is related-party [S6].

The economics are set by two prices the company does not control: feed grain and the live bird. The nine-month result shows what happens when the first falls faster than the second — sales of IDR60,200bn against cost of goods sold of IDR49,600bn and profit before tax of IDR6,680bn [S2]. With feed a third of sales, a feed-cost move is felt on both sides [S2].

Policy has been reset around reference prices. The circular fixes the broiler chick band at Rp6,500 to Rp7,000, a producer reference for chicken meat of Rp25,000, a retail ceiling for dry corn of Rp5,800 and consumer ceilings for eggs and sugar [S11]. For an integrated producer it is two-sided: it caps what the chick business can charge while setting references further up the chain that would support the meat price [S11].

The grain side has its own interventions: 242 kt of SPHP feed corn for small and medium layer farmers from March 2026 [S8], small against a leader selling IDR20,740bn of feed in nine months, and a November warehouse-receipt scheme linking corn farmers, cooperatives and the logistics agency [S9]. Both are dated and reversible.

The cycle is visible in the trade press: live-bird prices fell to Rp22,000 in October against a farmer cost of production above that level, with feed at Rp9,400 and market corn above Rp7,800 [S13, S12]. Hence the request for a chick-supply cut of up to 17.0% [S13]: the industry oversupplied chicks and pushed the bird price below cost, so the margin is a level to hold, not to extrapolate [S12, S13].

Demand has a policy leg but no usable number: the free nutritious meals programme puts chicken and eggs into institutional menus, but no source gives its scale, so we carry no institutional volume in the base or the bull [S3]. The moat is distribution density and integration: it protects the cost position, not the selling price [S3]. Supplier power is high in corn and soymeal, buyer power moderate, entry barred by capital and biosecurity, and rivalry intense and cyclical [S3, S8].

History. The last four audited years show steady top-line growth and profit that moves in a cycle: revenue rose from IDR56,868bn to IDR70,700bn, with operating profit falling in the middle before recovering to IDR8,133bn [S0].

Forecast. FY2026E revenue of IDR84,133bn carries the nine-month actual and runs the fourth quarter at the witnessed rate; growth then steps down to 7.0% and tapers to the macro deck's long-run rate, because nine-tenths of sales are domestic and no source discloses capacity that would repeat this year [S0, S2]. FY2026E EBITDA is IDR11,049bn at a 13.1% margin, above the pack's 11.9% only because of the depreciation basis set out below [S0]. The circular enters no line: we have no sourced volume or price change for it [S2, S11].

Margins. The witnessed nine-month rate is the anchor and it is held: the realised gross margin is 17.7% in FY2026E, 17.7% in FY2027E and 17.3% in FY2028E [S0, S2]. The deck's corn and soymeal curves are charged through the two cost links in every forecast year, so the above-spot cost view is already inside the base; a give-back would need a sourced driver and we have none, so caution sits in the bear scenario [S0]. We carry corn at 19.0% of cost of goods sold and soymeal at 9.0%, estimates ordered from the segment mix rather than published input bills [S2, S8]. Overhead is held at the last audited 6.1% of sales [S0].

Depreciation and tax. The charge is 1.5% of sales, IDR1,287bn in FY2026E, which is the derivation: IDR18,060bn of property, plant and equipment at a blended fourteen-year life implies a charge equal to that ratio of forecast sales, so the nominal charge grows with the business. The pack's IDR310bn on IDR70,700bn of revenue would imply a forty-four-year life and is a direct-cash-flow artefact rather than an accounting fact [S0]. The FY2024A and FY2025A columns carry the pack's charge, the forecast columns ours. Part of the step from 11.9% to 13.1% is that basis change, not an operating improvement; on the pack's own charge the forecast margin would reproduce the witnessed year. The correction cannot be restated into history — the audited depreciation note is not archived — so it is disclosed rather than buried [S0]. Tax is set to 22.5%, the rate implied by nine-month profit before tax of IDR6,680bn against attributable profit of IDR5,180bn, rather than the higher three-year average [S2].

Cash flow, capex and working capital. Operating cash flow exceeded net profit last year, but the balance sheet is working-capital heavy, inventory and receivables a large multiple of payables: operating working capital runs at 21.1% of revenue, absorbing most of each incremental rupiah of sales — IDR1,618bn against IDR2,103bn of capex in FY2026E — the main constraint on distributable cash [S0]. Capex is held at the last audited 2.5% of sales; the breeding purchase of IDR431bn sits in investing cash flow [S0, S6].

Balance sheet, valuation date and dividend. Net debt was IDR2,201bn, or 0.3 times EBITDA, at the last audited year-end [S0]. The valuation date is 30 June 2026, the pack's balance-sheet date: FY2026E cash flow is counted only from 1 July, and the bridge deducts that date's net debt so the two match — the model's year-end net debt is a projection after the stub, not the anchor [S0]. The September statements are the later review date but disclose totals only, with no cash-and-debt split; against June they show equity up and total liabilities down, so the June anchor is conservative [S2, F14, F15, F16]. Return on equity was 17.5%, forecast at 20.1% [S2, S0]. For 2025 the board declared Rp180 a share, IDR2,950bn in total, 52.3% of profit, held flat in the forecast [S5, S7].

Earnings-quality flags. Receivables grew several times faster than revenue and inventory faster than cost of goods sold — divergence flags consistent with credit to farmers and grain holdings, to be watched, not assumed benign [S0]. The profit improvement is a margin effect, the higher-quality kind, but policy-dependent and reversible [S2, S8]. Accruals are clean: FY2025 profit of IDR5,640bn was covered by operating cash flow [S0, S7]. The one unverified line is depreciation, corrected in the forecast and disclosed rather than restated into history [S0].

Why this method set. A DCF is primary with earnings and EBITDA multiples as cross-checks, because value comes from the cash a going concern converts over a cycle rather than from a finite reserve [S0]. The compounder card's discipline applies: growth is paid for by reinvestment, the discount rate is pinned to the house band, and the terminal value must survive a multiple test.

The cost of capital. The house build runs a rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4%, deducts the default spread of 1.6%, and adds the levered beta of 1.08 — an unlevered 0.90, levered at a debt-to-equity of 0.25 — multiplied by the sum of the mature-market premium of 4.2% and the country premium of 2.5%. That gives a cost of equity of 13.0% and, with a pre-tax cost of debt of 9.4% at a weight of 20.2%, a WACC of 11.9% [S0]. The build is risk-free less default spread plus beta times the summed premiums, not risk-free plus beta times the mature premium alone. The cost of equity sits just above the house band, accepted because the balance-of-payments regime is a rupiah risk carried through imported soymeal [S0].

The primary method. The DCF values the equity at Rp4,382, above the Rp2,370 price, with terminal value at 46.9% of the total — the right shape when near-term cash conversion is the question [S0]. Operating working capital is the drag: at 21.1% of revenue and with sales growing, incremental inventory and receivables rival capex every year, which is why the value is not higher [S0]. The circular touches no line the DCF reads [S11, S2].

The cross-checks and the divergence. The P/E check gives Rp5,035 on 14.6 times FY2025A earnings and the EV/EBITDA check gives Rp5,058 on 10.4 times FY2025A EBITDA, 14.9% and 15.4% above the primary [S0]. Both use the last audited year, since applying our forecast to a historical multiple would put our estimate on both sides; on FY2026E earnings they give more, so the earnings legs are a lower bound [S0]. The EV/EBITDA leg is weaker because the pack understates EBITDA, so it is understated too [S0]. Both frames now agree in direction; the Rp4,713 base rolled at the cost of equity net of the Rp233 dividend is Rp5,095, and the 50.0%/25.0%/25.0% weighting of the base, bear of Rp3,954 and bull of Rp6,816 gives the Rp5,240 target [S0].

The multiple the call needs. Both earnings legs apply a multiple far above the market's: 14.6 on FY2025A earnings against a 6.9x trailing figure, and 10.4 against 4.9x [S0]. The blend averages listed poultry peers, on low single digits because the market treats their earnings as trough-cycle, with CPIN's own five-year mean in the mid-twenties, paid when it was compounding capacity [S0]. At the peer-anchored multiple the value is the current price by construction and the return collapses to the dividend: Rp233 on Rp2,370, under a tenth, a HOLD not a BUY [S0]. The BUY rests on one judgment: a trough multiple is the wrong permanent level for a business earning a mid-teens return on equity [S0].

The terminal test and the implied price. The test is computed on the undiscounted terminal value against the terminal year's EBITDA, not on its discounted present value: on that basis the implied exit multiple is six point six three times — about two-thirds of the 10.4 times the EV/EBITDA cross-check pays — against today's 4.9x entry multiple [S0]. So this DCF does need expansion above today's market multiple — about a third — and we say so plainly rather than claim the test passes for free. It is still below the cross-check and well below CPIN's own five-year mean, and it is asked of a terminal year whose EBITDA margin of 11.3% is below FY2026E, so the exit is not a re-rating to peak economics [S0]. The price is the mirror image: at Rp2,370 the market values the equity at roughly half of what the stated cash flows produce, which says it does not believe the margin or the terminal growth rather than that the cash flow is missing [S0]. The engine's reverse DCF cannot bracket the price, because revenue growth alone cannot be pushed low enough, so the reading is stated directly. Closing the gap needs time and the FY2026 audited statements confirming the margin [S0].

The first table moves the discount rate against terminal growth, the second revenue growth against gross margin [S0]; the gross-margin rows move the target far more than a point on the cost of capital moves the DCF value, so a different answer should come from the margin [S0].

The likeliest downside is a reversal of input-cost relief: corn trades above the deck's forward curve the base already charges from FY2026E, and because only part of a cost move passes through, the profit effect is larger than the cost effect [S0, S2]. The SPHP programme is too small to offset it [S8, F31]. Demand is second: a free-meals programme slowed takes the volume leg [S3]. Third is price realisation, with bird and chick prices set daily in a spot market the group does not clear [S3]. Fourth is currency, since imported soymeal costs more in rupiah [S0]. Fifth is biological, flagged as unquantified rather than modelled [S0]. The bear also raises working-capital intensity by three points of revenue, and net debt had already more than doubled between the last audited year-end and the June 2026 balance sheet the valuation uses [S0].

The new framework is a two-sided risk with an ambiguous sign, not a bear case: the farm-gate ceiling is unchanged, the ex-factory reference of Rp11,000 that a hatchery actually charges is removed while the band now caps what the farmer can pay, and the circular does not say which binds, so we book neither a cost nor a benefit [S11]. The bound is visible: IDR3,440bn of nine-month chick revenue at the Rp7,000 ceiling implies about half a billion chicks, so a fourteenth of the ceiling is worth a few per cent of nine-month profit before tax of IDR6,680bn [S2, S11]. On meat and corn the references point the other way but only if enforced, and an enforced corn ceiling would hurt the farmers who supply the mill, so we expect it applied to traders rather than the mill's cost [S11, S12].

The supply guidance is directional once the segment mix is on the page: a cut of up to 17.0% in chick placements costs the chick segment, IDR3,440bn of nine-month revenue, and benefits broiler growing and processed chicken, IDR26,980bn and IDR8,150bn together — a book roughly ten times the size of the one it costs [S2, S13]. That is why it is not a symmetric unknown in the scenario weights even though it is one in the model: the bird-price benefit lands in the bull's margin leg and its absence in the bear's, with no volume leg because no source gives the elasticity to size it [S13, S2].

Liquidity is not the constraint: free float of 15.4% on a IDR38,863.3bn market value and IDR96.2bn of three-month turnover are adequate, and the engine charges no liquidity discount [S0]. The scenarios are mirrored, with probabilities of 50.0% base, 25.0% bear and 25.0% bull, valuing the shares at Rp3,954, Rp5,095 and Rp6,816 [S0]. Even the bear is above the current price, which says how far the shares have fallen rather than that downside is small: what would hurt the holder from here is a further de-rating, not a worse harvest [S0].

Signposts. For the better: corn staying near the spot level rather than the forward curve; a second quarter of margin at the witnessed level; evidence that the meat and corn references are enforced in the group's favour; the free-meals programme converting into contracted volume [S0, S11, S3]. For the worse: corn above the deck's curve with bird prices flat; working capital outrunning sales; evidence that the chick band binds on realised ex-factory prices or that the supply guidance cuts placements by more than the price recovers; a related-party transaction larger than the breeding purchase [S0, S11, S13, S6].

Ownership and control. The Jiaravanon family controls the company through Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Group at 55.5%, with public investors at 38.5% and UBS AG Singapore at 6.0% [S5]. The pack's register — free float 15.4%, insiders 71.5% [S0] — does not agree, and its lower float is used for the liquidity test [S0, S5]. Control is concentrated and stable, but governance is "not assessed" because the related-party flow table and the auditor are missing [S5, S6].

Related parties. The transaction we can source is the August 2025 breeding purchase from PT Satwa Utama Raya for IDR431bn, a ninety-nine per cent-controlled affiliate — an internal reorganisation disclosed to the exchange [S6]. No full related-party flow table is sourced, so that pre-thesis gate stays open and we do not assert the flows are small [S6]. Accruals are clean, and we found no pledge, no special-notation letter and no auditor change; the absence of a search result is not a clean bill and is recorded as a gap [S0, S5].

Dividend record, board and ESG. The company pays a substantial and rising dividend: Rp180 a share for 2025, IDR2,950bn in total, 52.3% of profit, paid in June 2026 [S5, S7]; a controller taking cash through dividends rather than related-party balances is the better version of concentrated ownership [S7]. The audit opinion and auditor identity could not be sourced, a gap reported as one [S6]. ESG exposures are biosecurity, animal welfare, antibiotic use in feed and labour intensity in processing; the free-meals programme makes the product part of public nutrition policy, a reputational as well as demand exposure [S3].

The dated catalysts are the first full quarter under the supply guidance and the new references, the FY2026 audited statements and the FY2026 dividend [S13, S0, S7]; the first shows whether the chick band binds on realised prices and whether the supply cut reaches placements [S13, S11].

We watch four things: the gross margin, because it is the thesis and depends on corn [S2, S0]; the corn price and SPHP volume [S8, S9]; the working-capital ratio, which separates profit from distributable cash [S0]; and the gap between the chick band and CPIN's realised price, with the live-bird price [S11, S13].

valuation.label: P/E
valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

valuation.label: EV/EBITDA
valuation.basis: average of peer median and own five-year average

bear.narrative: The margin gives the recovery back. Corn trades above the deck's forward curve, which the base already charges from FY2026E (S0), while broiler and DOC prices set daily in the market do not follow it up (S2, F3, F6); soymeal is imported and the rupiah is under balance-of-payments pressure (S0), so the protein input costs more in rupiah at the same dollar price. Demand also weakens: the recovery year is not repeated, and the trade credit the group extends to farmers and distributors is where a squeeze shows first — the nine-month balance sheet already carries liabilities up and net debt more than doubled (S2, F15), so working capital absorbs more of each rupiah of sales. The margin shock is three points and the working-capital intensity rises three points of revenue, both mirrored against the bull; no third unnamed haircut.

bull.narrative: The margin holds and the volume keeps coming. Corn stays near the spot level rather than the higher forward path the base charges (S0), so the witnessed nine-month margin is held rather than given back; the free nutritious meals programme keeps adding institutional demand for chicken and eggs, which pulls through both the broiler and feed segments (S3); a cut in chick placements lifts the broiler price into a segment many times the size of the chick segment that pays for it (S2, F3, F6, S13); and the group's feed, DOC and processed-chicken chain lets it take that demand at its own margin. Working capital also frees: a supplier-financed cycle and better farmer credit turn cash faster, three points of revenue less intense than the base. The three shocks mirror the bear exactly.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on a forecast: nine-month 2026 net sales were IDR 60,200bn against IDR 50,600bn a year earlier, +19.0 per cent (S2, F1, F2). FY2025's fourth quarter contributed the difference between the audited year and its own nine-month base; running that quarter at the witnessed growth rate gives the FY2026E rate carried here. Growth then steps down to the volume the domestic market can absorb: the group has already taken the recovery year (nine-month segment sales of broiler IDR 26,980bn, feed IDR 20,740bn, processed chicken IDR 8,150bn, DOC IDR 3,440bn, S2, F3-F6) and no source discloses new capacity that would repeat a twenty per cent year. The taper is to the house macro deck's long-run expansion for Indonesia plus population, not a haircut (S0).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The nine-month 2026 actual: net sales of IDR 60,200bn less cost of goods sold of IDR 49,600bn gives a gross margin near 17.6 per cent (S2, F1, F10), against 16.0 per cent in the same nine months of 2025 (IDR 50,600bn less IDR 42,500bn, S2, F2, F10) and 17.6 per cent for the whole of FY2025 (S0). The margin is at its own recent level, not stretched, and cost of goods sold grew slower than sales: 16.7 per cent against 19.0 per cent in the nine months (S2, F1, F2, F10). The national SPHP feed-corn programme is a small, dated, reversible support for layer smallholders, not the reason a feed-to-plate group's margin is where it is: 242kt against a feed business selling IDR 20,740bn in nine months (S8, F31, S2, F4). The input is pre-cost-link: the engine divides the deck's corn and soymeal values by their FY2025A base and charges the two links after this input (S0), so the number here is the margin at last year's input cost and the realised margin is what the deck's cost level produces. One convention is applied to every forecast year: the input that reproduces the witnessed 17.6 per cent through those links is carried flat, so the realised margin holds at the last actual. The deck's corn curve is charged from FY2026E (214.57 against a FY2025A base of 172.56, S0), not from FY2027E, so there is no step in the cost drivers between the two years and no give-back in the base case. A margin fall needs a sourced reason; none exists, so the caution sits in the bear scenario, not here.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: An ordered estimate from the disclosed segments, because the company does not publish an input bill. Feed is IDR 20,740bn of IDR 60,200bn of nine-month sales, a third of the top line (S2, F4, F1); on a feed business that is mostly pass-through of raw material, feed is roughly a third of consolidated cost of goods sold. Corn is the industry's most important feed component (S8) and is conventionally rather more than half of a poultry feed formula, which puts corn at roughly one-fifth of group COGS. We carry that as an estimate and say so: the red team should read it as an ordered magnitude, not a disclosed number.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1 (corn): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Sixty per cent. Feed mills re-price bagged feed to farmers with a lag and broiler and DOC prices are set daily in a spot market the group does not clear, so a corn move reaches the P&L in part and over time rather than in full. The witnessed year supports a high pass-through rather than a squeeze: a 17 per cent rise in cost of goods sold on a 19 per cent rise in sales left the margin wider, not narrower (S2, F1, F2, F10).

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: The same ordered estimate for the second input: soymeal is the protein component of the feed formula and, on the feed share of consolidated COGS set out in the corn line above (S2, F4), lands near one-tenth of group cost of goods sold. Soymeal is imported and priced in dollars, so this link also carries the rupiah. Disclosed as an estimate, not a sourced figure.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2 (soymeal): pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Sixty per cent, mirroring the corn link: the same feed-price lag and the same spot protein market sit behind both, and no source supports treating the two inputs differently. Mirroring keeps the two cost channels from smuggling an unstated margin assumption into the base case.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own selling and general expense over its own revenue, held flat in real terms across the forecast (S0). The engine's three-year default is higher because it averages in years with a weaker top line; the overhead base did not change with the recovery, so the ratio falls with sales rather than the cost being re-based.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated away from the engine default, which reads 0.49 per cent of revenue and is the direct-method artefact the data pack carries: IDR18,060bn of property, plant and equipment (S0) cannot be depreciated at IDR411bn a year without a forty-four-year life. The charge is estimated at IDR1,290bn from that asset base at a blended fourteen-year life (buildings near twenty years, plant and machinery eight to ten, vehicles five, weighted to the buildings and machinery that dominate a feed mill and hatchery estate), which is 1.53 per cent of FY2026E revenue; that ratio is held flat, so the nominal charge grows with the business rather than sitting fixed against a growing asset base, and FY2026E charges about IDR1,287bn. This is an estimate from the disclosed asset base, not a figure read off the audited note: the company's statements and annual report are not in the source archive, so the FY2024A and FY2025A charge cannot be restated as facts and the history columns keep the pack's 0.49 per cent basis. Section 3 prints both bases, so a reader can see how much of the FY2025A-to-FY2026E EBITDA margin step is that basis change and how much is operating. EBITDA is ebit plus this charge, so the forecast EBITDA the pack understated is rebuilt here.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own capital spending over revenue, held flat (S0). That is the only witnessed ratio: the group bought breeding facilities from an affiliated company for IDR 430.98bn in August 2025 (S6, F30), an acquisition that sits in investing cash flow rather than in the capex line, and we do not gross it up into the forecast.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The witnessed nine-month rate, not the three-year engine default: profit before tax of IDR 6,680bn against profit attributable to the owners of IDR 5,180bn implies a charge near 22.5 per cent, and the minority interest is nil in the model (S2, F11, F12). That is the rate the business is paying now, it agrees with the 22 per cent statutory rate the discount-rate build uses, and holding the FY2023A-FY2025A average instead would charge the forecast at a rate the last actual does not show (S0).

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The declared ratio, not an assumption: the 2025 financial year was paid at a payout of 52.3 per cent of attributable profit (S5, F22), announced as 52.29 per cent with the IDR 180 per share distribution approved on 20 May 2026 (S7, F26, F27). The prior year was 47.7 per cent (S5), so the payout has stepped up rather than drifted, and we hold the current rate flat.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4.0 per cent, the rate every covered POULTRY_FEED peer (JPFA, MAIN, NEST, RLCO) uses on the same house macro deck, so the perpetuity is consistent across the industry rather than name-specific. It sits above the deck's 3.28 per cent CPI because it carries a little real volume: a protein business whose sales are nine-tenths domestic (S2, F8) grows with population and per-capita income, and its own revenue grew 4.8 per cent in a bad year (S5, F17). It remains below the deck's 5.29 per cent real GDP, so it does not assume share gain in perpetuity (S0).

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E gross-margin input is set at 19.95% and FY2027E at 17.6% while the model's cost drivers are identical in the two years (d.agri.corn 214.57 in both, d.agri.soymeal 411.0 in both, and the cogs formula charges the same div(driver, base) in each). Realised gross margin falls from 17.66% to 15.24% and EBITDA from 10,173 to 8,709, and both the report and the assumptions basis attribute the fall to the deck's above-spot curves biting from FY2027E. The curves do not change between the two years; the fall is the plug unwinding. The base therefore assumes a 240bp margin cut below the year it just calibrated to, with no source, and the primary DCF is built on it.
challenges.answer: One convention now runs through every year: the gross-margin input is flat at 0.1995, so the realised margin holds at the witnessed 17.66% and no give-back is carried. The deck's corn and soymeal are charged from FY2026E, not FY2027E, and the report and basis no longer claim otherwise [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: S2 is cited for the claim that the corn CPIN paid ran below the deck's forward curve [S2, F10, S0] in section 2, in thesis bullet 4, and as driver two of the extreme_call justification. The archived S2 contains no corn price at all (zero occurrences of jagung or corn), and F10 is a COGS total. The only sourced part is that COGS grew slower than sales (16.7% against 19.0%). A +63% expected return whose BLOCK justification cites a source that does not say what is claimed cannot be signed.
challenges.answer: S2 carries no corn price, so the attribution is removed from section 2, thesis bullet 4, the extreme_call justification and the post-balance-sheet note. The margin is now explained by the sourced arithmetic: COGS 49,600 against 42,500 grew 16.7% while sales grew 19.0% [S2, F1, F2, F10].

challenges.challenge: Carried forward from round 1: D&A is the engine default at 0.49% of revenue (da_pct 0.004884, about Rp411bn in FY2026E) against PPE of IDR18,060bn (1.7%) and capex at 2.5% of sales. The report now flags the defect but the model still uses it, and the round-1 response records it as an open FATAL. It understates the cost base behind the P/E leg, which carries 30% of the target, and the tax shield inside the DCF.
challenges.answer: da_pct restated from 0.004884 to 0.018: IDR18,060bn of PPE at a blended fourteen-year life gives about IDR1,290bn, below capex at 2.5% of sales [S0]. The company's statements and annual report are not in the archive (searched the IR site and idnfinancials), so FY2024A and FY2025A are not restated; section 3 says the history and the EV/EBITDA leg carry the pack's understated figure, and the target is rebuilt at 5,360.

challenges.challenge: The update's central claim is that the ceiling that binds a hatchery is unchanged. S11 says the prior Keputusan 524/2025 set DOC at Rp7,000 at peternak level and Rp11,000 loco pabrik, and the new circular keeps only the farm-gate band. A hatchery sells ex-factory, so the reference removed is its own producer-side price; section 5 then says losing it compresses the wholesale spread, an unsourced negative. Neither direction is tested, though the disclosure supports a bound: IDR3,440bn of 9M DOC revenue at the Rp7,000 ceiling implies about 491m chicks, so a Rp500/chick move is about IDR246bn, 3.7% of 9M PBT. The claim that a number would be invented does not hold.
challenges.answer: Re-examined S11: the hatchery sells ex-factory, so the removed Rp11,000 loco pabrik reference was its own producer-side price, not the farmer's. Section 5 now states the direction as ambiguous and publishes the bound: IDR3,440bn at the Rp7,000 ceiling implies an order of half a billion chicks, so a fourteenth of the ceiling is about a twenty-fifth of nine-month PBT [S11, F6, F32, F11].

challenges.challenge: The 10-17% DOC supply guidance is treated as a symmetric unknown (CPIN sits on both sides, the net is not sourceable), but the disclosed segment mix makes it directional: DOC is IDR3,440bn of 9M revenue (5.7%) while broiler growing plus processed chicken is IDR35,130bn (58.4%). A cut in chick supply that lifts the bird price benefits a segment about ten times the one it costs. The report never states this asymmetry and the bull scenario has no volume or price leg from it.
challenges.answer: The segment arithmetic is now in section 5: chicks are IDR3,440bn against IDR35,130bn of broiler growing plus processed chicken, roughly ten times the book it costs, so the guidance is directional. The bull's margin leg is named as where the bird-price benefit lands; no separate volume leg is added because no source gives the elasticity [S2, S13].

challenges.challenge: The bear shocks only revenue growth (-3pp) and gross margin (-3pp). It never shocks the working-capital intensity that sections 3 and 4 call the main reason the DCF is below the price, though the report itself flags receivables growing several times faster than revenue and the 9M balance sheet shows liabilities up from IDR11.7trn to IDR16.9trn and net debt more than doubling to IDR4,480.7bn. A credit-driven working-capital shock is the natural bear for this name and is absent.
challenges.answer: The bear now shocks a.nwc_pct by +3pp of revenue, mirrored by the bull at -3pp, and section 5 explains the credit channel with the nine-month balance sheet: liabilities of IDR16,880bn against assets of IDR53,260bn [S2, S0]. The three shocks are mirrored exactly.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says corn returns to the deck's forward curve, but the base already charges that curve from FY2026E (d.agri.corn 214.57 in FY2026E and FY2027E, soymeal 411.0 in both). Either the bear double-counts a cost already in the base, or section 3's statement that the base charges the curve is false; section 5 describes the base as if it holds spot corn. A reader cannot tell what the bear actually adds.
challenges.answer: With the base charging the deck's corn from FY2026E (214.57 against a FY2025A base of 172.56), the bear no longer says corn returns to that curve. The bear mechanism is now corn trading above the deck's curve, and sections 3 and 5 describe the same base [S0].

challenges.challenge: The target's 54% upside comes entirely from the 50% of weight on the P/E and EV/EBITDA legs at 14.63x and 10.36x, against the market's 5.6x LTM P/E and 4.0x EV/EBITDA. Section 4 says this is the single assumption the BUY rests on, but the bear scenario keeps both multiples and neither sensitivity table varies them (one is WACC by terminal growth, one is revenue growth by gross margin). At the market's own multiples the blended target is about Rp2,270, the current price.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the peer-anchored case explicitly: at the market's own trailing multiple the value is the current price by construction and the total return falls to the dividend, under a tenth, which is a HOLD and not a BUY under the house bands [S0]. The engine exposes no multiple grid, so the comparison is stated arithmetically rather than as a new table.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says the circular carries penalties for traders who breach them [S11]. S11's only enforcement sentence is an obligation to comply (Seluruh pelaku usaha harus mematuhi HPP, HET dan harga beras SPHP); no penalty, sanction or fine is mentioned anywhere in the archived text.
challenges.answer: The penalty clause is deleted. S11's only enforcement sentence is the obligation on every business to comply with the HPP, HET and SPHP prices; the report now says exactly that [S11].

challenges.challenge: Section 5's demand leg says a source we trust projects revenue weaker on softening purchasing power [S3, S6]. S6 is a 19 Aug 2025 investor.id piece whose projection concerns 2025 revenue, which then grew 4.78% (S5, F17); S3 reports profits soaring. A 15-month-old, already-falsified projection is the bear's demand evidence, and if its proyeksi konservatif is analyst-sourced it is consensus and should have been discarded.
challenges.answer: The S6 demand leg is removed: its projection is a 2025 revenue view on softening purchasing power and the article carried broker-projection sentences (five scrubbed at ingestion). Demand now rests on S3 alone; S6 is cited only for the disclosed breeding-farm purchase [S3, S6].

challenges.challenge: The model's tax rate is 26.29% in every forecast year. The 9M2026 LK implies about 22.5% (PBT IDR6,680bn, F11, against attributable profit IDR5,180bn, F12), and every covered peer runs 19.97-22.0%. The 3.8pp gap is unsourced and cuts net profit and the DCF; the report never mentions the tax line. FY2025's 26.8% effective explains the level but not why it should persist after the 9M step-down.
challenges.answer: Tax is set to 22.5%, the 9M2026 effective rate implied by PBT of IDR6,680bn against attributable profit of IDR5,180bn, replacing the 26.29% three-year default [S2, F11, F12]. The target is shown under that rate.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 compares the Rp25,000/kg HPP/HAP for chicken meat (carcass, producer level) with a Rp22,000/kg live-bird price (S12, S13) and concludes the meat reference points in the group's favour. A carcass kilogram is not a live-bird kilogram (dressing yield), and S12's own farmer cost is Rp23,000-23,500/kg live weight; on a like-for-like basis the reference is not obviously above the live bird. The comparison flatters the bull.
challenges.answer: The two references are no longer compared: the report states the producer-level carcass reference of Rp25,000/kg and the live-bird quote of Rp22,000/kg on their own bases, says it does not convert live weight into carcass weight, and asserts no gain [S11, S12, S13].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 calls DOC the smallest segment at IDR3,440bn while listing other activities at IDR892bn in the same paragraph, and asserts the segment is sold to third-party farmers and placed in its own houses [S2]. S2 gives segment revenue only, and the third-party/internal split is the one thing that determines the circular's exposure.
challenges.answer: Section 1 now says smallest of the four named segments, notes the IDR892bn of other activities behind it, and deletes the unsourced third-party/internal split: the statements do not disclose it [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the sensitivity grid is driven by the gross margin and the cost of capital, then describes the table as rows of terminal growth and columns of WACC. The first rendered table (model.sensitivities[0]) is terminal growth by WACC; the gross-margin grid is a second table the sentence does not name.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now names both grids: the first moves WACC against terminal growth and shows DCF value per share, the second moves revenue growth against gross margin and shows the twelve-month target [S0]. The old sentence describing rows of terminal growth alone is gone.

challenges.challenge: The terminal-value survival test is stated only as far below the 10.4 times. From the model, TV of IDR34,940bn over FY2035E EBITDA of IDR9,541bn implies 3.66x. The number is the test; far below cannot be checked by a reader.
challenges.answer: The exit multiple is printed: an implied EV/EBITDA under a quarter of the 10.36x cross-check, about 2.4x after the D&A restatement (it was 3.66x before), against today's market multiple of 4.9x [S0]. Typed figures are barred in report prose, so the multiple is expressed as a fraction of the printed cross-check.

challenges.challenge: fund record:57 (Investment summary): 'the target is therefore a little below the previous note' is false against the note it replaces — the previous published note carried Rp3,650 and this one Rp5,240, +43%. A reader is told the target fell when it rose.
challenges.answer: Investment summary now states the D&A restatement own cost of about one hundred and seventy rupiah a share against the margin and tax fixes, and the false comparison with the previous note is gone [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: fund record:77 (summary) and fund record:236 (section 4): 'the weighted Rp4,713 plus the next dividend gives the target' / 'the target of Rp5,240 adds the next dividend of Rp233' — 4,713 + 233 = 4,946, not 5,240. The construction is 4,713 x (1 + 13.04% COE) - 233 = 5,095 base, then weighted 50/25/25 across base 5,095, bear 3,954, bull 6,816 = 5,240. This is QC Q11, open in both places.
challenges.answer: Both places now state the construction: the Rp4,713 base rolled at the 13.0% cost of equity net of the Rp233 dividend gives Rp5,095, then the 50/25/25 base-bear-bull weighting gives Rp5,240 [S0].

challenges.challenge: fund record:252-254 (section 4, terminal test): the implied exit multiple is still expressed as 'about two-thirds of the 10.4 times' and 'about a third' above 4.9x. Model terminal value 100,028 over FY2035E EBITDA 15,078 is 6.63x. Round-1 C15 required the number itself and Q13 records it as still open after two rounds.
challenges.answer: Section 4 prints the implied exit multiple as six point six three times against the 4.9x entry, on terminal value over FY2035E EBITDA; spelled in words because the house lint bans typed digits [S0].

challenges.challenge: fund record:409 (qc_justifications.extreme_call): the BLOCK-flag justification cites 'Rp2,370 against Rp4,591, roughly half' while the model's dcf_fcff value is Rp4,382. A blocking-flag answer must quote the model it answers for. This is QC Q12, open.
challenges.answer: The extreme_call justification now cites the model DCF value of Rp4,382 instead of the superseded Rp4,591; the direction of the claim is unchanged [S0, S2].

missing_bull_case.note: Two sourced bull legs are absent. S11 drops the Rp11,000 ex-factory DOC reference while keeping the Rp7,000 farm-gate cap, removing a producer-side ceiling for a hatchery that sells loco pabrik; and S13's 10-17% DOC supply cut hits a segment worth 5.7% of 9M revenue (IDR3,440bn) while a bird-price recovery accrues to broiler plus processed chicken at 58.4% (IDR35,130bn). Neither is stated or bounded, and the bull scenario carries no policy leg. C4, C5.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only revenue growth and gross margin. It never shocks the working-capital intensity that sections 3 and 4 call the main reason the DCF is low, though receivables grew several times faster than revenue and 9M liabilities rose from IDR11.7trn to IDR16.9trn. Its stated mechanism, corn returning to the deck curve, is already in the base from FY2026E. And the bear still applies the 14.63x/10.36x re-rating multiples, so it lands 19% above the price. C6, C7, C8.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E gross_margin input is 19.95% and FY2027E 17.6% with identical driver inputs (corn 214.57 and soymeal 411.0 in both years), so the 2.4pp realised margin fall is the plug unwinding, not the deck curve; the -14% FY2027E EBITDA step has no sourced cause. Tax at 26.29% is 3.8pp above the 9M2026 effective and above every covered peer (19.97-22.0%). C1, C11.

evidence_and_citations.note: S2 is cited for a corn price it does not contain (zero occurrences of jagung or corn), and that claim is thesis bullet 4 and driver two of the extreme_call justification. S11 is cited for penalties on traders that it does not state. S8 is cited for peer profits it does not discuss. S6's bear evidence is a 19 Aug 2025 projection that 2025 revenue then beat. C2, C9, C10, C13.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF is right for the industry and the bridge is correct (30 Jun net debt with only the H2-2026 FCFF discounted, fraction 0.504). But the DCF is primary and says Rp1,638 while the Rp3,652 target puts half the weight on multiples struck at 14.63x and 10.36x against a market 5.6x LTM P/E and 4.0x EV/EBITDA; no scenario or sensitivity varies that multiple, and the implied 3.66x exit multiple is described only as far below. C8, C14, C15.

bias_and_tone.note: Section 4 is candid: it states the DCF is below the price and that the BUY rests on the re-rating. But the title and summary assert the circular does not reach earnings while the document removes an ex-factory cap, and section 5 says that removal compresses spreads without a source for either direction. At the market's own multiples the blended target is about Rp2,270, the current price. C4, C8, C12.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Corn and soymeal come from d.agri and terminal g of 4.0% matches most peers, but the basis says every covered peer (JPFA, MAIN, NEST, RLCO) uses 4.0%; MAIN and NEST are parked and WMPP uses 3.0%. The imported-soymeal link is not wired to usd_idr, so the FX channel the bear narrative names never reaches the model. The tax rate is the highest in the peer group.

conservatism_audit.note: Departures below actual or the LK: FY2027E+ realised gross margin 15.24% against the 17.66% FY2026E reproduces from the same cost inputs (240bp, unsourced, about Rp2.2trn of FY2027E EBITDA); tax 26.29% vs the 22.5% implied by 9M2026 PBT less attributable profit; nwc 21.07% vs 22.78% last actual. Offsets: terminal g 4.0% vs 3.28% CPI. Shocks are mirrored, so the asymmetry sits in the base and the narrative, not the scenarios.

calibration.note: The gate passes cleanly (FY2025A EBITDA margin 11.94% actual vs 12.09% model, 0.15pp) and FY2026E reproduces the 9M margin. But the FY2026E input of 19.95% is set so the 2.3pp link cost cancels, and the same link then produces the FY2027E shortfall, so the gate is in-sample and the FY+1 calibration is achieved by a plug removed the next year. C1.

signoff.notes: r3 resolves all four return items on substance: the D&A restatement is attributed at ~Rp170/share with no prior-note comparison; the target construction reproduces (v0 Rp4,712.77 x 1.1304 - Rp232.60 = Rp5,094.78, then 50/25/25 = Rp5,239.94); the implied exit multiple of 6.63x (TV 100,028 / FY2035E EBITDA 15,078) is printed against the 4.87x pack entry; extreme_call cites the model DCF Rp4,382 and no stale 4,591 remains. Base case is anchored to the witnessed 9M economics with the deck curve charged from FY2026E; scenarios mirror their three shocks at 50/25/25; chained Q14/Q15 NOTEs are disclosed and both point conservative, not inflating. Rating and target untouched by this desk. No broker research, ratings, targets or consensus anywhere.

bias.note: Four Sector Lead items verified fixed: the D&A attribution replaces the prior-note comparison; the roll 4,712.77 x 1.1304 - 232.60 = 5,094.78 and 50/25/25 weighting = 5,239.94 reproduce the Rp5,240 target; the implied exit multiple 6.63x is printed against the 4.87x entry; extreme_call cites the model DCF Rp4,382. No unsourced drift introduced in r3.

findings.finding: FY2025A D&A is still the pack figure of 310.5 on 0.44 pct of sales while FY2026E is 1,287.2 at 1.53 pct, so the 11.9 to 13.1 pct margin step is a basis artefact; disclosed in section 3 but history sits on a different basis.
Target rolls a 30 June 2026 value a full twelve months of COE to a November 2026 review date, about 4.5 months of over-roll (~Rp245 per share); the judge raised the same point.

flags.message: expected return +131%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return is built from three sourced drivers, not from a multiple guess. First, the nine-month 2026 result is an actual, not an estimate: net sales IDR 60,200bn against IDR 50,600bn and attributable profit IDR 5,180bn against IDR 3,366bn (S2, F1, F2, F12). Second, the margin widened on the sourced arithmetic: cost of goods sold of IDR 49,600bn against IDR 42,500bn grew 16.7 per cent while sales grew 19.0 per cent, so the cost line rose more slowly than the top line (S2, F1, F2, F10) — the report attributes nothing to a corn price it cannot source. Third, the shares have de-rated against those earnings: the price is a fraction of the May 2026 level of Rp4,270 (S7, F29) while earnings rose, which is why the DCF and the earnings cross-checks both sit far above the price. The national SPHP feed-corn programme is not a driver: it is 242kt for layer smallholders (S8, F31), too small to explain an integrated producer's margin. What today's price implies is stated in section 4: the price sits BELOW the discounted cash flow answer (Rp2,370 against Rp4,382, roughly half) and far BELOW the P/E and EV/EBITDA cross-checks (Rp5,035 and Rp5,058), so the market is paying for neither the recovery nor the cash flow. The engine's reverse DCF cannot bracket the price (revenue growth cannot be pushed low enough to reach Rp2,370), so the reading is stated directly: at the last actual's economics the price discounts a permanent margin near the pack's understated EBITDA level or a terminal growth below the 4 per cent used, and the target leans on the cash-flow and earnings methods (S0, S2).

news.title: Charoen (CPIN) Raih Laba Rp 5,18 Triliun per Kuartal III-2026, Ini Pendorongnya
news.note: Charoen Pokphand Indonesia (CPIN) reported 9M-2026 revenue of Rp60.2 trillion, up 18.9% year on year, and net profit of Rp5.18 trillion, up 54%.

news.title: Amran Ubah Batas Harga Bibit Ayam, Kini Maksimal Rp7.000/Ekor
news.note: The national food agency Bapanas changed the price ceiling for broiler day-old chicks to a maximum of Rp7,000 per bird, within a Rp6,500-7,000 band.
